bullets.title: AI capex selloff: semis -9.5%, AI bottlenecks -14% w/w; hyperscaler earnings are the reset catalyst
bullets.body: The week's dominant theme was a violent unwind of the AI trade—SOX fell as much as 7% in single sessions (worst since 2022), with AI infrastructure names down 12-20% from early-October peaks. Drivers: rising neocloud credit stress (CRWV 2031 notes ~16% yield), OpenAI/Anthropic revenue misses vs. expectations, Korean neocloud IPO Elice -32% on debut, and META's capex disclosure (FY26 guided to $135-145B, with 'hundreds of billions' language for multi-year). GS prime: hedge fund AI allocations fell from 99th to 94th percentile; $20B net TMT selling over two weeks. Despite the selloff, earnings fundamentals were generally constructive—TSMC/ASML reported healthy results; TXN, WDC, BE all beat-and-raised.

bullets.title: META Q3 beats but -9% w/w on capex/equity raise overhang; Muse traction real
bullets.body: META delivered 3Q revenue of $64.6B (+26% YoY) with Q4 guide $73-76B, but stock fell ~9% on capex guidance ($135-145B for 2026 vs prior range) and revelation of a non-voting Class C share structure for future capital raises. Muse reached 10M+ US/Canada users in ~6 weeks with 25% daily engagement and 25% shopping use at >$200 avg purchase. Sell-side majority bullish—Mizuho raised PT to $950, Citi to $905, MS maintained OW at $820. Key bear risk: META's 5yr CDS hit a record 114.5bps, and 2027 capex estimates vary from $200B (consensus) to $250B+ (Morgan Stanley bull case).

bullets.title: NFLX -6% on ad revenue cut and engagement concerns; Wolfe downgrades to Peer Perform
bullets.body: Netflix Q3 EPS $0.87 beat but Q4 guide disappointed—ad revenue outlook cut to $2.7B from ~$3B due to slower rollout, and Q4 op margin of 26% included 120bps headcount charge. Content chief Bela Bajaria replaced by Peter Rice; film chief Dan Lin also fired. US watch time growth lagging; global Top-10 viewing hours fell 11% in Q3. Wolfe downgraded to Peer Perform; MS cut PT to $77 (OW maintained); Needham downgraded to Hold. Stock down ~46% YTD.

bullets.title: WDC crushes Q1FY27—revenue +55% YoY, Dec quarter guide $5.1B vs $4.6B street; HAMR on track
bullets.body: Western Digital reported F1Q27 revenue $4.38B (+5.8% above consensus), EPS $4.64 (+13% beat), GM 58.1% (+240bps above). F2Q guide of $5.1B and 60-61% GMs was ~10-11% above Street. HDD supply-demand imbalance persists with customer visibility through CY2030-31; HAMR qualification in F1Q27 with volume shipments H1 CY27. Demand broadening beyond hyperscalers to neo-clouds and AI labs. JPM PT $668 (OW), Citi cut to $660 (Buy), MS raised to $668 (OW). Despite the quality of the results, stock was initially -4-6% on capex concerns.

bullets.title: SPOT Q3 beats on GMs, 4Q guide better than feared; MS raises PT to $700
bullets.body: Spotify Q3 premium net adds of 6M beat vs. 5M guide; GMs 33.0% beat guidance 32.9%. Q4 guide: revenue €5.2B inline, operating income €820M vs €804M consensus, GM 33.8% vs 33.5% est—driving +8-11% pre-market. AI Remix licensing deal with Believe/TuneCore seen as future monetization driver. MS raised PT to $700 (OW, ~30x FY28 FCF). Key debate: when marketing/AI spend normalizes.

bullets.title: CMCSA Q3 beats across board; broadband -144K net adds; NBCU spin mid-2027 on track
bullets.body: Comcast reported Q3 adj EBITDA $9.11B vs $8.89B consensus, EPS $1.07 vs $0.99, FCF $4.21B vs $3.44B. Residential broadband losses of -144K slightly better than feared but ARPU -2.9% YoY pressured by fiber/FWA competition. Peacock turned profitable at $261M EBITDA. Parks EBITDA down 17% YoY from Orlando softness—expected to recover 2H27. NBCU/Sky separation on track for mid-2027; buybacks paused. MS maintains EW $27 PT; KeyBanc UW at $18; Citi Buy at $27.50.

bullets.title: T beats Q3, raises FY26 EPS to $2.40; SpaceX wireless threat triggers -6% selloff
bullets.body: AT&T Q3 service revenue +3.8% YoY beat, EBITDA +5.4%, EPS $0.65 vs $0.60 consensus. Fiber adds +442K beat, FWA +327K beat; postpaid phone adds 379K slightly light. Raised FY26 EPS guide to ~$2.40 from $2.25-2.35, lowered 2027-28 capex to $22-23B. Stock fell 6-7% on SpaceX's concurrent announcement of plans to access 80K+ US cell sites (Crown Castle leading), positioning as a fourth wireless carrier. Wolfe maintains OW $29 PT; MS cut PT to $25 (OW).

bullets.title: NVDA: Hedgeye removes long on Rubin delay; supply chain announces 2.5x capacity expansion
bullets.body: Hedgeye removed its NVDA long position citing Rubin mass production delay to Q2 2027 from expected Q4 2026/early Q1 2027. Separately, NVDA announced a major supply chain buildout: SPIL optical engines +15x by mid-2027, Amkor +300% interposer capacity, KYEC $1.1B testing facility, Samsung Electro-Mechanics new fabs, and substrate capacity +2.5x over 3 years. NVDA trend signal remains mixed—Hedgeye bearish trend, while bulls argue GTC Berlin confirmed strong 2027 demand. GTS TorchNeuron/TorchTPU open-source releases lower AWS/GCP switching costs vs NVDA.

bullets.title: CRM acquires Braze for $5.66B (60% premium); strategic but execution risk flagged
bullets.body: Salesforce agreed to acquire Braze at $47.50/share (~$5.66B EV, ~5x CY27 revenue) to strengthen Marketing Cloud with real-time mobile engagement. Deal funded with cash, no debt; closes in Salesforce FY28 (Feb-Jan 2027). No change to FY27 guidance. JPM maintains OW on CRM; KeyBanc neutral; Wolfe OW at $360. Early feedback mixed—acquisition fills a product gap but pace of M&A and integration risk flagged. HUBS, INTU, NOW rallied in sympathy.

bullets.title: AAPL: Hedgeye and Loop Capital bearish at 38x P/E; iPhone Duo supply constrained but in demand
bullets.body: Two negative catalysts this week: Loop Capital downgraded AAPL to Hold (PT $330 from $370) citing iPhone shipment reductions; Hedgeye maintained short thesis at 38x FY2027 P/E with single-digit growth expected. iPhone Duo (foldable) sold out on day one with 94-day lead times globally—Apple raised shipment targets 44% to ~14M units in first 12 months. China non-premium share losses flagged as 'critical red flag.' Pro lead times normalized to ~7-8 days inline with prior year. Nov 2 earnings guidance risk highlighted.

bullets.title: MU: Buy thesis intact—HBM4 in HVM, $35B buyback, union strike risk averted
bullets.body: Micron HBM4 confirmed in high-volume manufacturing with HBM4E samples shipping; NAND skipping G10 to jump to G11 targeting 2H27 ramp with 2x density improvement. $35B share buyback announced (largest in company history). Taiwan union planned strike was averted after Taichung labor agreement signed. Citi hosting investor meetings reiterating Buy. The stock held flat w/w vs SOX -3.2%, showing potential bottom formation on bad news according to Citi TMT desk.

bullets.title: MRVL: Hedgeye top pick; $30+ FY2031 EPS, $1T valuation thesis; MSFT Maia key driver
bullets.body: Marvell Investor Day outlined $30+ EPS target for FY2031 with a path to $1T valuation, making it Hedgeye's top semiconductor pick. UBS notes MSFT Maia 300 entering multi-GW-scale deployment in 2027 is a key upside catalyst for MRVL custom silicon. Hedgeye simultaneously removed the ANET short. XPO/NPO (active optics) preferred over CPO in their hierarchy.

bullets.title: STX: JPM sentiment +5 (max bullish), preferred over WDC; Q1 consensus $4.14B vs guide $4.1B
bullets.body: JPM survey shows STX at maximum bullish sentiment (+5), favored over WDC on HAMR transition leadership and stronger near-term execution despite trimmed target multiples to mid-teens. UBS also sees STX beating Sept/Dec quarters on HAMR ramp and higher ASP. Consensus Q1 revenue $4.14B vs guidance $4.1B ±$100M; EPS $7.42 vs $7.30 guidance. Options imply ~11.4% move. Reports Oct 27.

bullets.title: GLW: JPM trims PT to $165 on valuation; tracking toward Springboard $20B/quarter a quarter early
bullets.body: Corning is tracking toward its $20B/quarter Springboard revenue run-rate a quarter ahead of schedule, driven by enterprise optical demand growing >75% YoY. JPM trimmed PT to $165 from $170 (Neutral) on 'lofty valuation' at 27x 2028E EPS. UBS sees 3Q at $0.90-0.93 vs guidance $0.85-0.89 with positive setup on lower investor expectations. LightCounting raised 2028 TRx market outlook +40%; GLW's DCI business has $1B+ revenue optionality. Reports Oct 27 BMO.

bullets.title: CLS Investor Day preview: JPM models $38.9B 2027E revenue (80%+ YoY), $485 Dec-27 PT
bullets.body: JPM's preview for Celestica's Investor Day expects management to guide FY2027 revenue ~$38.9B (+80%+ YoY, vs Street $35.7B) with ~9% operating margins and potential ~$3B FCF outflow on heavy capex/working capital. Dec-27 PT $485, implying 59% upside. UBS also constructive with Buy $430 PT: expects Sept quarter beat and strong Dec guidance on hyperscaler switch/TPU demand; Oct investor day may outline ~$19 CY27 EPS. CLS reports Oct 26.

bullets.title: DKNG: NY sportsbook GGR +79% YoY on hold rate expansion; UBS Buy $48 PT
bullets.body: New York OSB data for week ending Oct 18: DKNG handle growth +5% YoY (accelerating from +4%), GGR +79% YoY driven by hold rate of 10.0% (+410bps YoY, +80bps week-over-week). October MTD GGR +24% YoY on +3% handle. Market share 33% (down 290bps YoY as Fanatics gained share). UBS maintains Buy $48 PT at 17x 2028E EBITDA. Week 6 NFL outcomes were favorable for operators with ~10-12% estimated hold.

bullets.title: RCL: MS constructive; NCLH downgraded to Underweight by JPM with $11 PT
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley is constructive on RCL—bookings pacing ahead of historical levels at record pricing with 4Q yield guidance +3.7% vs Street +4.7%. JPM downgraded NCLH to Underweight (PT $11 from $13) citing a 180bps unfavorable spread between net yields and net cruise costs ex-fuel, FY27 adj EPS of $0.91 vs consensus $1.49, and Caribbean pricing weakness. Fuel costs rising ~20% in bunker prices weigh on both.

bullets.title: NOW: Jefferies most positive setup of the week; stock up 73% since prior earnings, doubles off lows
bullets.body: ServiceNow is up 73% since the day after its last earnings report and has doubled off its lows, with Jefferies calling it the most upside print follow-through of the week. JPM expects ~200bps cRPO beat and +50bps guidance acceleration from partner checks. AI ACV on track to exceed $1.5B target. Wolfe and JPM both bullish ahead of Oct 28 print (consensus $4.09B revenue, $1.02 EPS). Key risk: stock up significantly makes bar high.

bullets.title: CART: exploring sale at $16-17B valuation (30-40% premium); DASH and UBER in talks
bullets.body: Multiple sources confirm Instacart (CART) is exploring a sale with talks from both DoorDash and Uber, with a valuation of $16-17B implying a 30-40% premium to the prior trading price. Separately, eBay announced a ~9% workforce reduction (~1,000 employees), expected to drive MSD% EPS uplift in 2027. RBLX faces LSD-MSD% bookings headwind in Q4 from GTA VI launch (estimated 45-62M units).

bullets.title: GEV moved to active short by Hedgeye; AI power trade rolling over on margin risk and political headwinds
bullets.body: Hedgeye moved GE Vernova to an active short and Cummins to their top short, arguing 'sold out through 2030' signals peak orders and margin risk, not a bullish thesis. Rate-of-change math cuts equipment sales even when the market doesn't shrink; fixed-price contracts face margin risk as backlog growth peaks. Political headwinds: ~70% chance of Democratic sweep priced in, and 39% of Americans believe AI does more harm than good. Macro timing: Quad 4 in 1Q27 historically bearish for capital equipment. BE (Bloom Energy) raised guidance for a third consecutive quarter—$4.4-4.6B revenue vs $4.1B consensus—but stock fell on capacity expansion concerns.
